description: The exact contents of the Time Series database (which tables exist, at what frequency, whether any payment-instrument tables are included, and file formats) could not be enumerated because the page is Cloudflare-protected.

Cash usage in the narrow sense (currency in circulation / cash withdrawals as a share of transactions) is only weakly covered. Kosovo unilaterally uses the euro and does not issue currency, so there is no domestic currency-in-circulation series; cash intensity must be proxied via ATM withdrawal volumes and the cash-vs-card split in CBK payment data.
No per-bank or per-scheme (Visa/Mastercard) breakdown of card, ATM or POS activity was found in CBK output; published data appears sector-aggregated.
No release calendar for CBK statistics was located, so publication timing must currently be inferred from observed file dates and news items.

This cell deliberately stops at the CBK. Adjacent statistical compilers that would triangulate CBK figures — the Kosovo Agency of Statistics (ASK / Agjencia e Statistikave të Kosovës), the World Bank Global Findex and Kosovo's national payments infrastructure operator — were seen only in passing and are not documented here.
The contents of the two highest-value CBK endpoints (the payment-systems statistical publications page and the Seritë kohore portal) are unknown because the domain refuses plain fetches.

Confirmed payment artefacts are annual (Use of Bank Cards, Annual Report) or semi-annual (FSR); the quarterly repository files (Tremujor/Tromesecni) are of unknown vintage and may be discontinued legacy.
E-banking and mobile-banking USER counts (as opposed to transaction counts) are only weakly sourced — one figure appeared via annual-report summaries; no dedicated recurring series was identified.
Cash usage (currency in circulation, ATM withdrawal values as a share of payments, cash-in-transit/branch cash handling) is only indirectly covered by this cell's findings.

Serbian-language coverage was productive at the portal level but no Serbian-language payments statistics document unique to the sr mirror was identified beyond the legacy Tromesecni files and KosGIRO manual.
No commercial/industry-side actor (card scheme, acquirer, processor, fintech/PSP register) was pinned down for XK payments infrastructure.

Albanian-language vendor terminology for this cell is thin and partly borrowed from English ('POS', 'terminale', 'bankomat'), and no Albanian-language vendor press room was found — Kosovo integrators appear to publish mostly in English or on LinkedIn.

The local reseller/service layer that physically installs and maintains ATM/POS estates in Kosovo is not yet enumerated; only CACTTUS and the ASEE/Payten and Printec regional entities were identified.

Vendor deployment announcements for this market increasingly appear on LinkedIn company pages rather than corporate newsrooms (the one confirmed Kosovo Printec win surfaced on Facebook, not the website).

The strongest Kosovo vendor evidence found is from 2016 (Quipu/Compass Plus contactless) and an undated Printec/BPB post; there is little recent (2023-2026) vendor-side quantification of Kosovo deployments.

Cash-management suppliers (CIT companies, cash-centre automation, note sorters such as Giesecke+Devrient or Glory) serving Kosovo were not covered in this pass, though they are directly relevant to cash-usage intelligence.
Kosovo's Albanian-language TV/radio economy desks (Klan Kosova, RTK, T7, Dukagjini, Kohavision) were not confirmed by search; broadcast interviews are a known origin of otherwise-unpublished figures.

Several major Kosovo Albanian portals with economy desks did not appear in this pass — notably Gazeta Express, Indeksonline, Insajderi, Nacionale, Zëri, Bota Sot, Reporteri, Gazeta Blic, and Kosovo 2.0 (bilingual, analytical).

No Albanian-language media reporting was surfaced on fintech / e-money institution licensing, instant payments, or the BQK payment-system modernisation programme — topics that typically drive payment-market change stories.
No archive/back-catalogue strategy was established for Kosovo portals, several of which restructure URLs or drop old articles; dated figures could become unretrievable.
Serbian-language Kosovo outlets yielded nothing in this pass despite the run scope including sr.

No Serbian-language academic or university source (e.g. economics faculty of the Priština University seated in Kosovska Mitrovica) was identified, despite it being the natural producer of peer-reviewed work on the northern-Kosovo payments economy.

Commercial banks' own Serbian-language disclosures for their northern branch networks (NLB Komercijalna, ProCredit, Raiffeisen Kosovo, Banka Ekonomike) were not directly inspected; only third-party press descriptions were found.

Coverage skews to the four northern municipalities; Serbian-majority enclaves south of the Ibar (Gračanica, Štrpce, Ranilug, Klokot, Novo Brdo, Parteš) are thinly represented by only one or two outlets.

No regulatory/legal-text source was captured for the Serbian side (foreign-exchange and payment-transaction regulations governing whether and how Serbia may transfer euros or dinars toward Kosovo), which was referenced in commentary but not located as primary text.

International-organisation Serbian-language reporting (EU/EUSR, OSCE Mission in Kosovo, UNMIK, IMF Article IV) on banking access in Serbian-majority areas was not sampled in this pass, though several of these bodies publish in Serbian.
Retrieved material clusters heavily around the 2024 dinar-ban episode; 2025-2026 follow-up on how payment behaviour settled after the transition period is under-represented.

Serbian-language research infrastructure in Kosovo (University in Kosovska Mitrovica economics faculty, Serb-community think tanks such as New Social Initiative, Aktiv, Center for Peace and Tolerance) was only partially mapped.

Kosovo private-sector and association research (Kosovo Banking Association analytical notes, chambers of commerce economic surveys, Kosovo Bankers' School) was not covered under this academic-focused cell but overlaps with it.
Key sources (bqk-kos.org, ResearchGate) require browser-grade fetching; naive HTTP harvesting will misclassify them as unavailable.

No academic or think-tank source found that specifically reconstructs ATM/POS terminal density or acquiring economics for Kosovo; academic work concentrates on consumer adoption attitudes rather than infrastructure series.

Conference proceedings series (notably the annual UBT International Conference, hosted in the same knowledgecenter platform) were not enumerated, though they routinely include Kosovo banking/payments papers.
The cash-in-transit / cash-management / ATM-replenishment operator class in Kosovo is entirely unmapped: no register, no named operators, no local-language search term that works.

No verified count or geography of MTO cash pay-out points exists yet. UFP claims 170+ UnionNet/Western Union locations and MoneyGram's locator implies several hundred agents, but neither figure is independently confirmed and overlap between them is unknown.
Posta e Kosovës branch/counter count, financial-service transaction volumes and any MTO partnership are not published on the accessible pages.

Serbian-language coverage in this cell rests mainly on BQK's ?lang=sr editions and Serbian media reporting on BQK releases; no Serbian-language Kosovo commercial or municipal source (e.g. northern-municipality MTO agents, Serbian-language postal or payment services) was located.

Survey evidence indicates cash carried in person during family visits is the dominant remittance channel, but no current, regularly-updated source measures this informal cash inflow. The most-cited figures trace back to UNDP remittance studies from earlier survey waves.

Remittance data by delivery instrument (cash pickup vs credit to account vs card/wallet) at the Kosovo level is only partially visible through BQK's channel split (non-bank financial institutions vs banks vs other), which is an institution split, not an instrument split.

The primary source domain (bqk-kos.org) returned 403 to automated fetching, and a mirror/staging host (bqk.hpdevenv.com) appeared in search results — indicating an unstable or duplicated site infrastructure that could break naive URL-based collection.
Serbian-language indirect channels for Kosovo (north-Kosovo bank branches, sr-language local media, sr job listings) are effectively uncovered.
Vendor-side weak signals are untouched: processor/switch/ATM-vendor press releases and case studies (card management, POS acquiring, ATM fleets) naming Kosovo banks as customers.
Cash-usage weak signals (cash-in-transit tenders, ATM cash-replenishment procurement, coin/banknote handling contracts) were not searched in this pass.
Job ads and conference agendas expire and are frequently removed, so the channel has no retrospective depth unless snapshotted at first sight.
Consumer-side complaint aggregators outside the regulator (consumer associations, the Ministry of Industry/Trade consumer-protection inspectorate, social-media complaint clusters) are unmapped.
No demand-side measurement of ATM withdrawal behaviour or cash-holding habits from the statistics office.

Serbian-language coverage of ASK content was confirmed to exist (/sr/ path, HIPC releases, metadata XML) but was not enumerated series-by-series; no Serbian-language third-party analyst source for Kosovo statistics was found.
PxWeb API endpoint pattern and rate limits for askdata.rks-gov.net are assumed from the standard PxWeb product, not confirmed.
Non-ASK official demand-side actors in this cell were not explored: the Kosovo tax administration (ATK) fiscal-cash-register/e-invoicing data and the telecom regulator (ARKEP) subscriber statistics.
International aggregators that republish and harmonise ASK series (Eurostat enlargement statistics, World Bank Findex, UNECE, IMF) were not covered in this cell.
Historical depth and archival redundancy of ASK's GUID-named PDF store is unknown.

Not every licensed Kosovo bank had its own report archive located in this run — Ziraat Bank Kosova and any remaining smaller/foreign-branch institutions are unresolved, and Banka Ekonomike's current annual-report PDF path was not pinned down (only its indicators page and a 2003 legacy PDF).

Per-bank card portfolio size (cards issued by type) and acquiring POS-terminal counts are confirmed only for TEB; ATM counts are stated in marketing prose for Raiffeisen ('over 160') and otherwise only implicitly enumerable from locator pages.
Most banks in the cell publish annually only; NLB is the exception with quarterly/interim statements already posted into 2026, and BKT's Albanian parent publishes periodic consolidated reports.
No sr-language commercial-bank disclosure identified; sq and en are the working languages of this cell.

Reports use inconsistent formats and metric definitions across banks (TEB reports a total POS terminal figure; others may report only branch counts or narrative digital-adoption claims), and file naming is unstable (BPB serves a generic 'Raporti-Vjetor.pdf').

Cell scope named six parent groups, but Kosovo also hosts foreign-owned banks/IFI-backed institutions outside the list (e.g. Turkish-owned Is Bank presence, IFI shareholders such as EBRD/IFC/KfW in ProCredit, and Albanian-owned non-bank payment players).

Credit rating agency reports and analyst notes on the parent groups (Moody's, Fitch, S&P) were not searched in this slice; they frequently contain subsidiary-level Kosovo commentary and peer market-share tables.
German-language sources (ProCredit Holding is Frankfurt-listed; RBI is Vienna-listed) were not searched, although the run's language set is sq/sr/en.
Back-series depth is uncertain: current IR sites expose roughly the last 5-8 years, while older Kosovo subsidiary reports appear only on third-party mirrors.
Group disclosures give Kosovo P&L and portfolio lines reliably, but cash-usage indicators (ATM withdrawal volumes, cash-in/cash-out) were not found at group level for any parent.

The definitive per-name list of Kosovo's licensed payment institutions and e-money institutions was not read, because the BQK register PDF returned 403. Named actors in this slice (Paysera Kosova, OneFor, Swinto/Velanis, Numarics) came from press and cluster membership, not from the register itself.

Only one processor with documented Kosovo operations (Quipu) and one regional vendor (Payten) were identified. The acquiring layer — who actually signs merchants and owns the POS estate in Kosovo — remains largely unmapped.
No route was established to the audited financial statements of non-bank licensees, which would carry transaction-linked revenue and sometimes volume disclosures.
Telecom-led payment channels (Vala/IPKO, Post and Telecom of Kosovo) as non-bank payment or e-money providers were not investigated beyond the postal payment-services page.

Albanian-language business media (Telegrafi, Insajderi, Kallxo, Ekonomia Online, albinfo.ch) repeatedly carried the only actor-level numbers found, but no systematic monitoring source was defined for them.
The Kosovo Banking Association member roster and any statistical bulletin it publishes were not read — the pages returned 403 to automated fetch.

E-money institutions and payment institutions (IPE/IP) were confirmed to be a regulated category with their own BQK regulations, but no dedicated per-category register page was isolated — only the combined dated list PDF.
No Serbian-language association or register index specific to Kosovo banking was found.
No Kosovo-specific pointer for card schemes/processors (Visa/Mastercard licensees, local processors, ATM network operators) was identified in this cell.
Terms of service and rate limits for the third-party ARBK mirrors (arbk.org, arbk.atlas-studio.eu) were not reviewed.
None of the listed URLs were fetched or liveness-tested in this pass; IMF's data portal in particular was recently re-platformed (data.imf.org) and older dataset endpoints may have moved.

Additional IFI/DFI actors publishing Kosovo financial-sector data were not explored in this pass: BIS (CPMI Red Book-type statistics), CEB, KfW/DEG, the Vienna Initiative, EFSE/Finance in Motion, and the World Bank Western Balkans Regular Economic Report series.
Serbian-language coverage of this cell is effectively empty and no useful sr-language IFI terminology could be established.
The Kosovo-specific World Bank retail-payment-cost study dates from February 2022; no more recent IFI demand-side cash-cost measurement for Kosovo was found.
Two of the highest-value datasets (Findex microdata, WB/EBRD Enterprise Survey microdata) sit behind registration or licence-request flows rather than open download.
Kosovo's presence or absence in EPC document EPC409-09 v8.0 (Dec 2025) was inferred from search snippets and regional announcements, not read inside the PDF.
The EC Kosovo Report 2025 PDF was identified but its Chapter 4/9/17/18 text was not extracted, so the exact payment-system and statistics findings for 2025 are not yet captured.

EU-funded technical-assistance projects touching Kosovo payments and statistics (IPA multi-beneficiary statistical cooperation, EU4 digitalisation/financial-sector projects, TAIEX/Twinning with CBK) were only glimpsed and not systematically mapped.

Other European bodies plausibly relevant to this cell were not searched: the European Banking Authority (Western Balkans cooperation/MoUs), the ECB's technical cooperation programmes with Western Balkans central banks, the Vienna Initiative full reports, and the Council of Europe Development Bank.
Albanian-language coverage of the EU/European layer is limited to translated EC reports; no Albanian-language European-body statistical product was found.
Only the most recent editions of most series were identified; the archive depth (EC reports back to 2008, Eurostat enlargement products, EBRD assessments) was not enumerated.
The CPV codes actually used by Kosovo contracting authorities for ATMs, POS terminals, card personalisation, payment switches and cash-handling equipment have not been enumerated.

The buyer roster for payment infrastructure was only partly built. Telekomi i Kosovës / PTK, Trusti i Kursimeve Pensionale, Administrata Tatimore e Kosovës (ATK), Thesari / Ministria e Financave, KEK/KESCO and regional water companies were identified as likely buyers but their individual procurement pages were not opened.
The supplier side of the channel — local system integrators and their reference/press pages announcing Kosovo public payment-infrastructure wins — was not scouted in this pass.
Portal continuity is not guaranteed — e-Prokurimi was reported inaccessible for six consecutive days, and donor notices (UNDP, IOM, EBRD) are routinely removed after closing.

Kosovo law requires notices in Albanian, Serbian and (above thresholds) English, but the multilingual notice versions on e-Prokurimi were not inspected, so it is unknown whether the sr/en versions carry the same technical annexes.
